Elena — thanks for the clear list. High-level approach and answers inline below, plus a proposed MAP and a suggested weekly cadence.

1) Backfill throughput
- We recommend a staged backfill: seed (1–2% of corpus) -> bulk (throttled by ingestion window) -> buffer sync. Typical run for your size: 8–12 hours for seed, bulk run over 24–72 hours depending on throttle and parallelism. Aim for ~3–6k inserts/min initially; we can ramp to 10k/min in Dedicated if needed.

2) Vector DB guidance
- Managed (Pinecone): easiest operationally + low-latency cloud SLA. Good if you want minimal ops and fast cutover.
- Self-managed (Milvus/FAISS): better if you need on-prem or strict networking; requires more ops and snapshot/replication planning.
- Redwood plays nicely with both; we'll recommend Pinecone for cloud-first migrations and Milvus if you need private deployments.

3) Rerank evals and acceptance gate
- Primary metrics: NDCG@5 (target >= 0.65), MRR (baseline +/− 0.02 delta), and 95th percentile token-generation latency for reranker < 120ms (post-cache).
- Run an A/B on a holdout query set (~1k queries) during canary. If NDCG delta is > -0.02 vs baseline we hold.

4) Downtime & cutover
- Canary with partial traffic is our standard. No full downtime required if you run prefix caching + a fallback model for the first 10–15% of traffic.

Next steps:
- I'll put together a MAP and a technical checklist. Can we do a 30m technical deep-dive on 2027-06-02 10:00 PT? I've attached a draft MAP (MAP_Atlas_v1.xlsx) and a link to the shared doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3cAtlasMAP

If this looks sensible I'll loop eng for a runbook and timing estimates.

Thanks,

Thanks for the ping — assigning owners and an outline of the runbook below.

Owners:
- Index backfill owner: Marissa Cole (implementation + monitoring)
- Vectorstore compatibility/ops: Karthik Iyer (schema, codec, deployment configs)
- Rerank eval harness: Vivek Kulkarni (offline eval infra + canary dashboards)

Implementation outline (PRD/runbook-level):
Phase 0 — Sampling & priming (pre-cutover)
- Take 0.5–1% seed sample from customer_data_profile.csv. Generate embeddings, validate length/embedding distribution.
- Prime caches with high-frequency prefixes.

Phase 1 — Seed index + verification (smoke)
- Insert seed (~12k vectors), run verification queries (50 known queries), validate NDCG and latency.
- Acceptance: NDCG@5 >= 0.65 on seed sample; insertion error rate < 0.1%.

Phase 2 — Bulk backfill (controlled rollup)
- Use block-based workers with checkpointing. Throttle to 5k inserts/min initially; monitor insertion latency (target < 200ms) and downstream ingestion lag.
- Create time-windowed snapshots every 30 mins for quick rollback.

Phase 3 — Canary / A-B traffic shift
- Route 10% of search traffic to new index for 48 hours (holdout queries + live traffic). Track NDCG/MRR and 95p latency. If NDCG delta <= -0.02, pause and investigate.

Phase 4 — Cutover & post-cutover reconciliation
- Gradually increase traffic, final sync for delta items, and finalize cutover window.

Operational metrics to publish on Redwood Console during rollout:
- Embedding generation throughput (vectors/sec), insertion throughput (docs/min), insert latency (p99/p95), rerank NDCG@5 & MRR on holdout, error rates, cache hit ratio.

Acceptance criteria (short):
- NDCG@5 >= 0.65 on holdout and delta vs baseline >= -0.02
- Insertion latency p95 < 200ms and error rate < 0.5% during bulk
- Post-cutover query latency within the customer SLA (95p < 200ms)

Smoke test window suggestion:
- Pre-cutover smoke: 2027-06-10 09:00–11:00 PT (seed verification + rerank holdout run).
